name: Adam
title: The first human being and the first prophet
story:
Adam, peace be upon him, is the first human being and the first prophet. The Qur'an tells us that Allah announced to the angels that He would place on earth a being entrusted with it. The angels wondered about a creature that might spread corruption and shed blood. Allah answered that He knew what they did not know.

Allah created Adam from clay and taught him the names of all things. When the angels were asked to give these names, they admitted that they knew only what Allah had taught them. Adam then named them. Knowledge was the first honour given to humankind.

Allah commanded the angels to prostrate before Adam. All obeyed except Iblis, who refused out of pride, claiming that he, created from fire, was better than a being made of clay. He was expelled, and he swore that he would try to mislead the children of Adam.

Adam and his wife were settled in the Garden. They could eat freely of everything, except from one tree. Satan whispered to them, swearing that he was a sincere adviser and promising them eternal life. They both ate from the tree. The Qur'an does not put the blame on the wife alone: it says that both of them slipped. Their nakedness became apparent to them, and they began to cover themselves with leaves of the Garden.

What followed is the heart of the story. Adam and his wife did not argue or make excuses, as Iblis had done. They turned to their Lord, admitted that they had wronged themselves and asked for His forgiveness and mercy. Adam received words from his Lord, and Allah accepted his repentance. The Qur'an says that his Lord then chose him, forgave him and guided him.

Adam and his wife were sent down to earth, where human beings would live, die and be raised again. Allah promised that guidance would come to them, and that those who follow it will have nothing to fear and will not grieve.

The Qur'an does not say where the Garden was, what kind of tree it was, or how long Adam lived, and there is no need to guess. What it does teach is that all human beings come from the same father and mother, and that the door of repentance has been open since the very first day.
lesson: Everyone makes mistakes; what matters is to admit them without excuses and to come back to Allah quickly. Pride closes the door that humility opens.

name: Idris
title: A man of truth raised to a high station
story:
Idris, peace be upon him, is one of the prophets about whom the Qur'an says very little. He is mentioned by name in only two places, and each time in a few words.

In Surah Maryam, after the stories of several prophets, Allah tells the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to mention Idris in the Book. He is described as a man of truth and a prophet, and the Qur'an adds that Allah raised him to a high station. In Surah al-Anbiya, he is named together with Ismail and Dhul-Kifl: all three were among the patient, Allah admitted them into His mercy, and they were among the righteous.

That is all the Qur'an tells us. It does not say when Idris lived, to which people he was sent, or what happened during his mission. Scholars have explained the high station in different ways: some understand it as a high rank and honour with Allah, others as a raised place in the heavens. In the sound hadith about the Night Journey, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ relates that he met Idris in the fourth heaven, and that Idris welcomed him (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3887).

Many later books add details: that he was the first to write with a pen, to sew clothes or to study the stars, or that he is the same person as a figure known from older scriptures. These reports do not come from the Qur'an or from sound hadith. They cannot be presented as established facts, and it is wiser to leave them aside.

What remains is short but precious. Out of a whole life, the Qur'an has kept three qualities: truthfulness, patience and righteousness. The Arabic word used for him, siddiq, describes someone who is deeply truthful, whose actions match his words and whose words match his faith. No account of power, wealth or fame is attached to his name; only his character has been preserved.

The few verses about Idris also remind us that a person's worth with Allah does not depend on how much people know about him. A prophet may be honoured in the Qur'an in two lines, and those two lines are enough to make him an example.
lesson: Be truthful and patient even when nobody notices: with Allah, character counts for more than fame.

name: Nuh (Noah)
title: The tireless caller and builder of the Ark
story:
Nuh, peace be upon him, was sent to a people who had fallen into the worship of idols. The Qur'an even gives the names of these idols: Wadd, Suwa, Yaghuth, Yauq and Nasr. Nuh came to them with a simple message: worship Allah alone, ask His forgiveness, and He will forgive you.

The Qur'an says that Nuh remained among his people for a thousand years less fifty. He called them night and day, in public and in private. He reminded them that Allah is ever forgiving and that He would send them rain in abundance. But the more he called, the more they turned away. They put their fingers in their ears and covered themselves with their clothes so as not to hear him.

The leaders of his people looked down on him. They said he was only a man like them, and that only the lowest people followed him. Nuh answered that he asked them for no wealth, that his reward was with Allah alone, and that he would never drive away those who believed.

When it was revealed to Nuh that no one else among his people would believe, Allah ordered him to build the Ark under His watch. The chiefs mocked him each time they passed by. Then the command of Allah came, and the flood began. Nuh was told to take on board a pair of each kind of creature, his family and those who believed, and they were only a few.

The Ark sailed through waves like mountains. Nuh saw one of his sons standing apart and called him to come aboard. The son answered that he would take refuge on a mountain. A wave came between them, and he was among the drowned. Nuh spoke to his Lord about his son, and Allah told him that this son was not truly of his family, because his conduct was not righteous. Nuh accepted this with humility.

Then the earth was ordered to swallow its water and the sky to hold back its rain. The Ark came to rest on Mount Judi, and Nuh was told to disembark in peace, with blessings upon him and those with him. The Qur'an says that the Ark was left as a sign for all people.
lesson: Keep doing what is right even when results are slow to come. Success is measured by faithfulness, not by the number of people who follow you.

name: Hud
title: The messenger sent to the people of Ad
story:
Hud, peace be upon him, was sent to the people of Ad, who lived in a region the Qur'an calls al-Ahqaf, the sand dunes. They came after the people of Nuh and had been given great strength. Hud was one of them: the Qur'an calls him their brother.

His message was the same as that of every prophet: worship Allah alone, you have no other god. He told them that he asked them for no reward. He invited them to ask forgiveness of their Lord and to turn back to Him, promising that Allah would then send them abundant rain and add strength to their strength.

The leaders of Ad answered harshly. They accused him of foolishness and of lying. Some even said that one of their gods must have struck him with evil. Hud replied calmly that there was no foolishness in him, that he was a messenger from the Lord of the worlds and a trustworthy adviser to them. He reminded them that Allah had made them successors after the people of Nuh, and he asked them to remember His favours.

Then he spoke words of great courage. He declared that he had nothing to do with the false gods they worshipped, and he challenged them to plot against him all together, without giving him any respite. He said he relied on Allah, his Lord and their Lord, who has power over every living creature.

The people of Ad did not change. They even asked Hud to bring the punishment he warned them about. One day they saw a cloud approaching their valleys and rejoiced, thinking it would bring rain. It was in fact a violent wind carrying a painful punishment. The Qur'an says that it blew against them for seven nights and eight days in a row, leaving the people lying like hollow trunks of palm trees. Afterwards nothing could be seen except their dwellings.

Hud and those who believed with him were saved by the mercy of Allah. The Qur'an does not tell us how many they were or where they went afterwards.

The story of Ad is told several times in the Qur'an as a warning to every powerful people: strength and prosperity are gifts, and they protect no one who uses them to reject the truth and to act with arrogance.
lesson: Strength, talent and wealth are gifts to be thankful for, not reasons to feel above others. When someone gives you sincere advice, listen before you judge.

name: Salih
title: The messenger sent to Thamud
story:
Salih, peace be upon him, was sent to the people of Thamud, who came after the people of Ad. They were skilled builders: the Qur'an says that they built palaces on the plains and carved homes out of the mountains. Salih was one of them, and before his mission his people had placed great hopes in him.

He called them to worship Allah alone. He reminded them that it was Allah who had brought them out of the earth and settled them on it, and he asked them to seek His forgiveness and not to spread corruption in the land. Their answer was disappointment: how could he forbid them to worship what their fathers had worshipped? They said they were in serious doubt about his message.

A few people believed, mostly among the weak. The proud leaders asked them, with contempt, whether they really thought Salih had been sent by his Lord. The believers answered plainly that they believed in what he had been sent with.

Allah then gave Thamud a clear sign: a she-camel. The Qur'an calls her the she-camel of Allah. Salih asked his people to let her graze freely on Allah's earth, to respect her turn to drink, and not to harm her, or else a punishment would seize them. The Qur'an does not describe how the she-camel appeared, and the detailed stories told about this are not established.

The test was simple, and they failed it. The Qur'an also mentions nine men in the city who spread corruption and who swore together to attack Salih and his family by night. The most wretched among them rose up, and the she-camel was hamstrung and killed. Then they defied Salih to bring the punishment he had promised.

Salih told them that they had three days left to enjoy in their homes, a promise that would not be denied. Then the punishment came: a mighty blast and an earthquake seized them, and they were left lifeless in their homes, as if they had never lived there. Salih and those who believed with him were saved by the mercy of Allah.

The Qur'an reports the last words of Salih as he turned away from them: he had conveyed to them the message of his Lord and given them sincere advice, but they did not like those who give advice.
lesson: A blessing is also a responsibility: respect what has been entrusted to you. Welcome sincere advice, even when it is not what you wanted to hear.

name: Ibrahim (Abraham)
title: The friend of Allah and father of the prophets
story:
Ibrahim, peace be upon him, grew up among people who worshipped idols and heavenly bodies. His own father, whom the Qur'an calls Azar, was one of them. From his youth, Allah had given Ibrahim sound judgement, and he could not accept that people should bow to statues they had made with their own hands.

The Qur'an tells how he reasoned with his people. He looked at a star, then at the moon, then at the sun. Each one set and disappeared, and each time he showed that something which disappears cannot be the Lord. He then declared that he turned his face towards the One who created the heavens and the earth.

One day, when the people had gone away, Ibrahim broke their idols into pieces, except the largest. When they questioned him, he told them to ask the big idol, if idols could speak. For a moment they realised how absurd their worship was. But pride won, and they decided to burn him. Allah commanded the fire to be cool and safe for Ibrahim, and he came out unharmed.

Ibrahim then left his people for the sake of his Lord and asked Him for a righteous child. In his old age, Allah granted him Ismail and Ishaq, and he gave thanks to the One who hears every prayer.

By the command of Allah, he settled some of his family in a valley without crops, near the Sacred House, and prayed that hearts would lean towards them and that they would be given fruits. Later, he raised the foundations of the Kaaba with his son Ismail. While they built, they asked Allah to accept their work and to send to the people of that land a messenger from among themselves.

Ibrahim was also tested in the hardest way: he saw in a dream that he was sacrificing his son. He told his son about it, and the son answered that he should do what he was commanded. When both had submitted, Allah called to Ibrahim that he had fulfilled the vision, and the son was ransomed with a great sacrifice. Muslims remember this every year at Eid al-Adha.

The Qur'an says that Ibrahim was tried by his Lord with commands and fulfilled them all, and that Allah made him a leader for people.
lesson: Use your mind to look for the truth, and have the courage to follow it even if you stand alone. What we give up for Allah is never lost.

name: Lut (Lot)
title: The prophet who stood firm among a corrupt people
story:
Lut, peace be upon him, lived in the time of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. The Qur'an says that he believed in Ibrahim's message. He was then sent as a prophet to a people whose city the Qur'an does not name.

These people had fallen into grave wrongs. The Qur'an says that they committed an indecency that no people before them had committed: the men approached men with desire instead of women. They also attacked travellers on the road and did evil openly in their gatherings. Lut called them to fear Allah and to give up these acts. He told them that he asked for no payment and that he was a trustworthy messenger to them.

Their only answer was to mock him and to threaten him. They said: drive Lut and his followers out of the city, for they are people who want to stay pure. They even challenged him to bring the punishment of Allah if he was telling the truth. Lut then asked his Lord for help against those who spread corruption.

Angels were sent with a mission. They first visited Ibrahim, to whom they brought good news of a son, and told him that they were going to the people of Lut. Then they came to Lut in the form of guests. He did not know who they were, and he was distressed, because he feared what his people would do to them. Indeed, the men of the city came rushing to his house. Lut begged them to fear Allah and not to shame him in front of his guests. He wished he had the strength to stop them.

The angels then revealed who they were: messengers of his Lord, whom the people would never reach. They told Lut to leave during the night with his family, and that no one should look back. His wife, however, would be among those who stayed behind and would share the fate of the others.

In the morning, the punishment fell. The city was turned upside down and stones of hard clay rained upon it. Lut and those of his family who followed him were saved.

The Qur'an says that the remains of that place were left as a clear sign for people who use their reason.
lesson: Doing right does not depend on what the majority does. Stay true to your values, even when you are mocked for wanting to stay pure.

name: Ismail (Ishmael)
title: True to his promise, builder of the Kaaba with his father
story:
Ismail, peace be upon him, is the son of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. Ibrahim had asked his Lord for a righteous child, and he thanked Allah for granting him Ismail and Ishaq in his old age.

The Qur'an reports the prayer of Ibrahim saying that he had settled some of his descendants in a valley without crops, near the Sacred House, so that they would establish prayer. A long hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari (no. 3364) relates how Ibrahim left Ismail, still a baby, with his mother Hajar in that empty valley of Mecca, how she ran between the hills of Safa and Marwa looking for water, and how the spring of Zamzam appeared. Pilgrims still walk between these two hills in memory of her trust in Allah.

The Qur'an then tells of a great test. Ibrahim saw in a dream that he was sacrificing his son, and he asked him what he thought. The son, described as gentle and forbearing, answered that his father should do as he was commanded, and that he would find him, if Allah willed, among the patient. When both had submitted, Allah called to Ibrahim that he had fulfilled the vision, and He ransomed the son with a great sacrifice. The Qur'an does not name the son in this passage; most Muslim scholars hold that it was Ismail.

Father and son then worked together on a task that still marks the life of Muslims. Allah charged Ibrahim and Ismail to purify His House for those who walk around it, stay there in worship, bow and prostrate. Together they raised the foundations of the Kaaba, asking Allah to accept this from them, to make them and their descendants people who submit to Him, and to send to the people of that land a messenger from among themselves. Muslims see in the coming of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, a descendant of Ismail, the answer to this prayer.

The Qur'an sums up the character of Ismail in a few words. He was true to his promise, a messenger and a prophet. He used to enjoin prayer and charity on his people, and his Lord was pleased with him. Elsewhere he is counted among the patient and among those whom Allah favoured.
lesson: Keep your promises, even small ones, and care about the faith of those close to you. Trust in Allah grows through patience in hard moments.

name: Ishaq (Isaac)
title: The good news given to Ibrahim in his old age
story:
Ishaq, peace be upon him, is the second son of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. The Qur'an tells the story of his birth in some detail, but says little about the rest of his life.

One day, guests came to Ibrahim and greeted him with peace. He returned their greeting and, generous as he was, quickly brought them a roasted calf. But the guests did not reach for the food. Ibrahim felt uneasy. They told him not to be afraid: they were angels, sent to the people of Lut, and they brought him good news of a son full of knowledge.

Ibrahim's wife was standing nearby. The Qur'an says that she was given the good news of Ishaq and, after Ishaq, of Yaqub. She was astonished: how could she have a child when she was an old woman who had never been able to bear children, and her husband was an old man? The angels answered: was she surprised at the decree of Allah? They wished the mercy and blessings of Allah upon the people of the house.

The promise came true. Ibrahim praised Allah for giving him Ismail and Ishaq in his old age, and declared that his Lord hears every prayer.

The Qur'an describes Ishaq as a prophet from among the righteous, and says that Allah blessed Ibrahim and Ishaq. It adds that Allah made Ishaq and Yaqub leaders who guided by His command, and inspired them to do good deeds, to establish prayer and to give charity; they were devoted worshippers of Allah. When Yaqub was close to death, his sons promised to worship the God of his fathers, Ibrahim, Ismail and Ishaq, one God.

Beyond this, the Qur'an gives no account of Ishaq's mission or of the events of his life. The many details found in other sources are not confirmed by the Qur'an or by sound hadith, so we do not repeat them here.

From Ishaq came Yaqub, and from Yaqub a long line of prophets among the Children of Israel, including Yusuf, Musa, Dawud and Isa, peace be upon them all. The birth of Ishaq shows that Allah keeps His promises in His own time, even when every visible cause seems to say that it is too late.
lesson: Never think it is too late for a prayer to be answered. Generosity towards guests and trust in Allah open doors that seemed closed.

name: Yaqub (Jacob)
title: The father whose patience was beautiful
story:
Yaqub, peace be upon him, is the son of Ishaq and the grandson of Ibrahim, peace be upon them. He is also known as Israil, and his descendants are called the Children of Israel. The Qur'an speaks of him mainly as a father, in the story of his son Yusuf.

When young Yusuf told him about a dream in which eleven stars, the sun and the moon bowed to him, Yaqub understood that Allah had chosen this child. He advised him not to tell his brothers, for fear that jealousy would push them to plot against him.

The brothers did plot. They asked to take Yusuf out with them. Yaqub said that it saddened him to let him go and that he feared a wolf might eat him. In the evening they came back in tears, with false blood on Yusuf's shirt. Yaqub did not believe their story. He told them that their own souls had led them to do something, and he chose beautiful patience, asking Allah alone for help.

Years passed. When a second son was kept in Egypt, the pain came back. Yaqub turned away and grieved for Yusuf, and his eyes turned white with sorrow, which he kept inside. His sons blamed him for still thinking about Yusuf. He answered that he complained of his sadness and grief only to Allah, and that he knew from Allah what they did not know.

Then he gave them this advice: go and look for Yusuf and his brother, and do not despair of the mercy of Allah.

His hope was rewarded. Yusuf, now a high official in Egypt, sent his shirt to be placed over his father's face. As the caravan left Egypt, Yaqub said that he could sense the scent of Yusuf. When the shirt was laid on his face, he could see again. His sons asked him to pray for their forgiveness, and he promised to do so. The whole family was reunited in Egypt.

The Qur'an also records Yaqub's last concern. As death approached, he asked his sons what they would worship after him. They answered that they would worship his God and the God of his fathers, Ibrahim, Ismail and Ishaq, one God.
lesson: Sadness is not a lack of faith: bring your pain to Allah and keep hoping. Never despair of His mercy.

name: Yusuf (Joseph)
title: The truthful one, from the well to the storehouses of Egypt
story:
The story of Yusuf, peace be upon him, fills a whole surah of the Qur'an. As a boy, he dreamed that eleven stars, the sun and the moon bowed to him. His father Yaqub, peace be upon him, told him to keep the dream from his brothers.

The brothers were jealous of their father's love for Yusuf. They took him out and threw him to the bottom of a well, then told their father that a wolf had eaten him. Travellers passing by drew Yusuf out of the well, and he was sold in Egypt for a few coins.

He grew up in the house of a high Egyptian official. When he became a man, the wife of this official tried to seduce him. Yusuf sought refuge in Allah and ran to the door; she tore his shirt from behind, which proved his innocence. Yet he was still sent to prison. He had even said that prison was dearer to him than what he was being called to do.

In prison, Yusuf was known for his goodness. He interpreted the dreams of two fellow prisoners and took the opportunity to speak to them about the one God. One of them was freed, but forgot to mention Yusuf to his master, and Yusuf remained in prison for several years.

Then the king had a dream: seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears of grain with others that were dry. Yusuf explained it: seven years of good harvests, then seven hard years, so the grain had to be stored. Before leaving prison, he asked that his innocence be established, and the wife of the official admitted the truth. Yusuf asked to be put in charge of the storehouses of the land, and he managed them carefully.

When famine came, his brothers travelled to Egypt for food. Yusuf recognised them, but they did not recognise him. After several journeys, he revealed who he was. They admitted their wrong. He answered that there was no blame on them that day and that he hoped Allah would forgive them.

Yusuf then brought his parents and all his family to Egypt. His childhood dream had come true. He ended with a prayer, asking his Lord to let him die in submission to Him and to join him with the righteous.
lesson: Stay honest and pure whether you are at the bottom or at the top. When you finally have power over those who hurt you, forgiveness is the noblest choice.

name: Ayyub (Job)
title: The model of patience
story:
Ayyub, peace be upon him, is the prophet whose name has become a symbol of patience. The Qur'an counts him among the prophets who received revelation and among the descendants of Ibrahim whom Allah guided.

The Qur'an tells his story in a few verses, without many details. Ayyub was struck by a severe trial that touched his health and his family. The Qur'an does not describe his illness, nor does it say how long it lasted. Many stories have been told about this, some of them exaggerated and unworthy of a prophet; they are not established and we leave them aside.

What the Qur'an has kept is the way Ayyub spoke to his Lord. He did not complain to people, and he did not accuse Allah. He simply called out that hardship had touched him, and that Allah is the Most Merciful of the merciful. In another passage, he says that Satan had afflicted him with distress and suffering. His prayer contains no demand: he describes his condition, he praises the mercy of his Lord, and he leaves the rest to Him.

Allah answered him. He told him to strike the ground with his foot: a spring of cool water appeared, to wash with and to drink. His suffering was removed. Allah gave him back his family and as many more with them, as a mercy from Him and a reminder for those who worship and for people of understanding.

The Qur'an also mentions that Ayyub had made an oath during his trial. Allah showed him a gentle way to keep his word without doing harm: to take a bundle of grass in his hand and strike with it. The Qur'an does not explain the circumstances of this oath in detail.

The passage ends with the praise of Allah Himself: He found Ayyub patient, an excellent servant, who always turned back to Him.

The patience of Ayyub was not silence or the absence of pain. He felt his suffering and said so, but he said it to Allah, with respect and hope. His story has comforted sick and grieving people for centuries, because it shows that a trial is not a sign of rejection by Allah, and that relief can come from where no one expects it.
lesson: In hardship, speak to Allah about your pain without losing respect or hope. Patience does not mean feeling nothing; it means staying faithful while it hurts.

name: Shuayb
title: The prophet of honest trade
story:
Shuayb, peace be upon him, was sent to the people of Madyan. The Qur'an calls him their brother, for he was one of them. It also mentions his preaching to the people of the Thicket; scholars differ on whether these were the same people as Madyan or a neighbouring group.

The people of Madyan were prosperous, but their trade was built on cheating. They gave less than was due when they measured and weighed, and they deprived people of what belonged to them. They also sat on the roads to threaten people and to turn the believers away from the path of Allah.

Shuayb called them first to worship Allah alone. Then he spoke to them about their daily business: give full measure and full weight with justice, do not cheat people of their goods, and do not spread corruption on earth after it has been set in order. He told them that what Allah leaves them as honest profit is better for them. He reminded them that they had once been few and that Allah had multiplied them.

Their answer was mocking. Did his prayer command him that they should give up what their fathers worshipped, or stop doing what they pleased with their own money? Shuayb answered with words that have remained famous: he did not want to do himself what he forbade them; he only wanted to put things right as far as he could, and his success depended on Allah alone, in whom he trusted.

He warned them not to let their opposition to him bring upon them a fate like that of the peoples of Nuh, Hud, Salih or Lut. He invited them to ask forgiveness, saying that his Lord is merciful and loving.

The leaders turned to threats. They said that they did not understand much of what he said, that they saw him as weak among them, and that without his family they would have stoned him. They threatened to expel him and the believers unless they returned to their religion.

The punishment came. The Qur'an speaks of an earthquake and a mighty blast that left them lifeless in their homes, and of the punishment of the day of the dark cloud. Shuayb and those who believed with him were saved by the mercy of Allah.
lesson: Faith shows in the way we buy, sell and work: give everyone their due. Practise what you ask of others.

name: Musa (Moses)
title: The one to whom Allah spoke
story:
Musa, peace be upon him, is the prophet most often mentioned in the Qur'an. He was born in Egypt at a time when Pharaoh oppressed the Children of Israel and had their newborn sons killed. Allah inspired the mother of Musa to place her baby in the river, promising to return him to her. Pharaoh's household picked him up, and Pharaoh's wife asked that he be spared. Since the baby refused every nurse, he was given back to his own mother to be fed.

As a young man, Musa struck an Egyptian who was fighting with a man of his people, and the man died. Musa had not meant to kill him; he regretted it at once and asked Allah for forgiveness. He fled to Madyan. There he helped two women to water their flock, then sat down in the shade and prayed that he was in need of any good Allah would send him. Their father welcomed him, gave him one of his daughters in marriage, and Musa worked for him for years.

On his way back with his family, he saw a fire near Mount Tur. There Allah spoke to him, made him His messenger and gave him signs: his staff turned into a snake and his hand shone white. Musa asked that his brother Harun be sent with him. Allah told them to go to Pharaoh and to speak to him gently.

Pharaoh refused to listen and summoned his magicians. But when they saw the staff of Musa swallow their tricks, they recognised the truth and declared their faith, in spite of Pharaoh's threats.

Allah then ordered Musa to leave by night with his people. Pharaoh chased them with his army as far as the sea. The people panicked, but Musa answered that his Lord was with him and would guide him. He struck the sea with his staff; it parted, and they crossed. Pharaoh and his soldiers were drowned.

Musa then went to meet his Lord for forty nights and received the Tablets. In his absence, some of his people began to worship a calf made from their jewellery. Musa came back angry and grieved, and called them to repent.

For the rest of his life, Musa led his people with patience, carrying the Torah, a guidance and a light.
lesson: Nobody is too weak to be chosen for something great, and no tyrant is too strong to fall. When you feel trapped, remember that Allah is with those who trust Him.

name: Harun (Aaron)
title: The brother and helper of Musa
story:
Harun, peace be upon him, is the brother of Musa, peace be upon him. In the Qur'an his story is always linked to that of Musa: he is the prophet who was given as a support to another prophet.

When Allah spoke to Musa and sent him to Pharaoh, Musa measured the weight of the mission. He asked his Lord to open his heart, to make his task easy and to loosen his tongue so that people would understand him. Then he asked for a helper from his own family: Harun, his brother, to strengthen him and to share his task. Musa said that Harun was more fluent than he was. Allah granted the request, and the Qur'an says that, out of His mercy, Allah gave Musa his brother Harun as a prophet.

The two brothers went to Pharaoh together. Allah had told them to speak to him gently, in the hope that he would remember or fear. They asked him to let the Children of Israel go and to stop tormenting them. When the magicians of Pharaoh saw the truth, they declared that they believed in the Lord of Harun and Musa.

After the crossing of the sea, Musa went to meet his Lord for forty nights. Before leaving, he asked Harun to take his place among the people, to act rightly and not to follow the way of those who spread corruption.

During this absence came the test of the calf. A man the Qur'an calls the Samiri led the people astray with a calf made from their jewellery. The Qur'an makes it clear that Harun did not take part in this. He told them that they were being tested by it, that their Lord was the Most Merciful, and that they should follow him and obey him. They refused to listen until Musa returned.

When Musa came back, angry and grieved, he seized his brother by the head. Harun answered him tenderly, calling him son of my mother. He explained that the people had overpowered him and had almost killed him, and that he had feared to divide the Children of Israel. Musa then asked Allah to forgive him and his brother and to admit them both into His mercy.

Elsewhere the Qur'an counts Harun among the prophets who were guided and rewarded for doing good.
lesson: Supporting someone else's mission is as noble as leading it. In a conflict with someone close, answer with gentleness and explain yourself calmly.

name: Dhul-Kifl
title: Counted among the patient and the best
story:
Dhul-Kifl, peace be upon him, is one of the figures about whom the Qur'an tells us the least. He is mentioned only twice, each time in a single verse and alongside other prophets.

In Surah al-Anbiya, he is named with Ismail and Idris. The Qur'an says that all of them were among the patient, that Allah admitted them into His mercy, and that they were among the righteous. In Surah Sad, he is named with Ismail and Al-Yasa, and the Qur'an says that all of them were among the best.

That is everything the Qur'an says. It does not tell us where or when he lived, to which people he was sent, or what he did. No sound hadith adds any clear detail about his life either.

His name itself has been discussed. In Arabic, Dhul-Kifl means something like the one with the portion, or the one who took on a commitment. Some commentators have suggested that he was given this name because he took on a heavy duty and fulfilled it faithfully, but this is an explanation of the word, not an established account. Others have tried to identify him with figures known from other traditions; these suggestions are guesses, and none of them rests on firm evidence.

Most scholars consider that he was a prophet, because the Qur'an names him and praises him among prophets. A few scholars have held that he was a righteous man rather than a prophet. In both views, he is a servant whom Allah Himself has praised, and that is the greatest honour.

It is worth noticing which qualities the Qur'an chose to mention. The first is patience: the ability to keep doing what is right over a long time, without giving up when things are hard. The second is righteousness. The third is to be counted among the best, in the company of prophets like Ismail and Al-Yasa.

So it is better to say honestly that we do not know the details of his life than to fill the silence with legends. The Qur'an does not always teach through long stories. Sometimes a name and a word of praise are enough to remind us that Allah knows His faithful servants, including those whose story no one has written down.
lesson: You do not need to be famous to be precious in the sight of Allah. Patience and faithfulness to your commitments are noticed by Him, even when nobody else sees them.

name: Dawud (David)
title: Prophet, king and devoted worshipper
story:
Dawud, peace be upon him, appears in the Qur'an for the first time on a battlefield. The Children of Israel, led by their king Talut, faced the army of Jalut. The believers were few, but they asked Allah for patience and firmness. They defeated their enemies by the permission of Allah, and Dawud killed Jalut. Allah then gave him kingship and wisdom and taught him what He willed.

Dawud became both a prophet and a king. Allah gave him the Zabur, the Psalms. The Qur'an describes him as a servant of great strength who constantly turned back to his Lord. When he glorified Allah, the mountains and the birds repeated the praises with him, in the evening and at sunrise.

Allah also made iron soft for him and taught him to make coats of armour with well-measured links, to protect people in battle. Although he was a king, a hadith tells us that Dawud ate only from what he earned by the work of his own hands (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2072).

His kingdom was made strong, and he was given wisdom and sound judgement in speech. But the Qur'an also tells of a moment when he was tested. Two men in dispute came into his prayer chamber and asked him to judge between them. Dawud gave his answer, then understood that Allah was testing him. He asked his Lord for forgiveness, fell down in prostration and repented, and Allah forgave him. The Qur'an gives no further details about this test, and the stories that have been added to it are not worthy of a prophet.

After this, Allah addressed him directly: He had made him a successor on earth, so he had to judge between people with truth and not follow his own desires.

The Qur'an also mentions a case about a field damaged at night by the sheep of some people. Dawud and his son Sulayman both gave a judgement, and Allah gave Sulayman the better understanding of the case, while both of them had received wisdom and knowledge.

Dawud thus brings together things we often think of as separate: power and humility, the skill of a craftsman and the devotion of a worshipper.
lesson: Whatever responsibility you hold, be fair and do not let your own wishes decide for you. When you realise you were wrong, turn back to Allah straight away.

name: Sulayman (Solomon)
title: The king who answered every gift with gratitude
story:
Sulayman, peace be upon him, was the son of Dawud, peace be upon him, and inherited from him prophethood and kingship. The Qur'an calls him an excellent servant who constantly turned back to Allah. He asked his Lord to forgive him and to grant him a kingdom such as no one after him would have.

Allah answered his prayer. He put the wind at his service, blowing by his command wherever he directed it. Jinn worked for him as builders and divers and made what he wanted. He was taught the language of the birds, and his army was made up of jinn, men and birds, lined up in ranks.

One day this army came to a valley of ants. An ant warned the others to go into their homes so that Sulayman and his soldiers would not crush them without noticing. Sulayman understood her and smiled. Instead of feeling proud, he asked Allah to help him be grateful for His favours and to do good deeds that please Him.

Another time, he noticed that the hoopoe was missing. The bird returned with news from Sheba: a queen ruled there, with a great throne, and she and her people bowed to the sun instead of Allah. Sulayman sent her a letter, which began with the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, inviting them to come to him in submission.

The queen consulted her advisers and chose caution. She sent a gift, which Sulayman refused: what Allah had given him was better. Before she arrived, her throne was brought to him in the blink of an eye by one who had knowledge of the Scripture. Seeing it in front of him, Sulayman said that this was a favour from his Lord, to test whether he would be grateful or ungrateful.

When the queen entered his palace, she took the floor of smooth glass for water. She understood that she had been mistaken about many things, and declared that she submitted, with Sulayman, to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.

The Qur'an also tells of his death. He died leaning on his staff, and the jinn kept on working, unaware of it, until a small creature of the earth ate through the staff and he fell. They then understood that they did not know the unseen.
lesson: The more you receive, the more grateful and humble you should be. Every ability is a test of what you will do with it.

name: Ilyas (Elijah)
title: The messenger who called his people away from Baal
story:
Ilyas, peace be upon him, is mentioned in two passages of the Qur'an. The first, in Surah al-An'am, names him in a list of prophets, together with Zakariyya, Yahya and Isa, and says that all of them were among the righteous. The second, in Surah as-Saffat, gives the short account of his mission.

The Qur'an says that Ilyas was one of the messengers. He spoke to his people and asked them whether they would not fear Allah. They worshipped an idol called Baal. Ilyas asked them how they could call upon Baal and abandon the best of creators: Allah, their Lord and the Lord of their forefathers.

His argument was simple and clear. The one who created them and created their ancestors before them is the only one who deserves to be worshipped. An idol has created nothing, and to turn to it is to forget the One to whom they owe their existence.

The Qur'an then tells us that his people rejected him. Because of this they will be brought to account, except the sincere servants of Allah. This means that some people, even if they were few, did listen to him and remained faithful.

The passage ends with a tribute. Allah left for Ilyas an honourable mention among later generations and sent peace upon him. He says that this is how He rewards those who do good, and that Ilyas was one of His believing servants.

The Qur'an gives no other details. It does not name the people of Ilyas, the land where he lived or the time of his mission, and it does not describe how his life ended. Commentators generally place him among the prophets sent to the Children of Israel, and other traditions tell long stories about him, but those accounts are not confirmed by the Qur'an or by sound hadith. We therefore keep to what is certain.

What is certain is already rich in meaning. Ilyas stood up in front of his people and asked them a question that every generation can ask itself: what do we put in the place of our Creator? The idol may no longer be a statue; it can be anything that we obey or love more than Allah. Many centuries later, his name is still spoken with a greeting of peace.
lesson: Ask yourself honestly what takes the first place in your heart. Speaking the truth is worth it even if only a few people listen.

name: Al-Yasa (Elisha)
title: Counted among the chosen and the best
story:
Al-Yasa, peace be upon him, is a prophet whom the Qur'an mentions only twice, and each time very briefly. There is no story about him in the Qur'an: only his name, placed among other prophets, and words of praise.

The first mention is in Surah al-An'am. After speaking of Ibrahim, Allah lists many of the prophets He guided. Among them come Ismail, Al-Yasa, Yunus and Lut, and the Qur'an says that Allah favoured all of them above all people. A little further on, the passage tells the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ that these are the ones whom Allah guided, and that he should follow their guidance.

The second mention is in Surah Sad. Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to remember Ismail, Al-Yasa and Dhul-Kifl, and says that all of them were among the best.

This is all that the Qur'an says about him. We are not told to which people he was sent, when he lived, what he said to his people or how they answered him. No sound hadith gives an account of his life. Commentators generally place him among the prophets of the Children of Israel, after Ilyas, and other traditions tell stories about him. Since these stories are not confirmed by the Qur'an or by sound hadith, we do not present them as facts.

It is better to accept this silence than to fill it. The Qur'an itself says elsewhere that there are messengers whose stories Allah has told and others whose stories He has not told. Believing in all the prophets does not require knowing the details of each life.

Still, the two verses teach us something. Al-Yasa is described as chosen, guided, favoured and among the best. These words are given by Allah Himself, who knows what is in every heart. And the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is told to follow the guidance of these prophets, which means that the way of Al-Yasa was the same as the way of all the others: to worship Allah alone and to do good.

His name in the Qur'an is like a quiet sign. It reminds us that the chain of prophets is long, that each of them carried the same message, and that many people who did great good are known fully only to Allah.
lesson: Do good without waiting for your story to be told. Being among the best in the sight of Allah matters more than being known by people.

name: Yunus (Jonah)
title: The man of the fish
story:
Yunus, peace be upon him, was sent as a messenger to a people who, according to the Qur'an, numbered a hundred thousand or more. The Qur'an also calls him Dhun-Nun, the man of the fish.

His story begins with a departure. Yunus left in anger. The Qur'an does not hide this: it says that he went off thinking that Allah would not put him in difficulty. Prophets are the best of people, and the Qur'an shows us how they return to Allah when they slip.

Yunus boarded a loaded ship. Lots were drawn on board, and he was among those who lost. He was cast into the sea, and a great fish swallowed him. The Qur'an says that at that moment he was to blame.

In the darkness, Yunus called upon his Lord. He declared that there is no god but Allah, glorified Him, and admitted that he had been among the wrongdoers. He made no excuse and blamed no one else. This short prayer is one of the most famous in the Qur'an.

Allah answered him and saved him from his distress, and the Qur'an adds that this is how He saves the believers. It also says that if Yunus had not been one of those who glorify Allah, he would have stayed in the belly of the fish until the Day of Resurrection.

He was cast onto an open shore, sick and weak, and Allah made a gourd plant grow over him. The Qur'an then says that he was sent to his people, that they believed, and that Allah let them enjoy life for a time. The Qur'an points out that the people of Yunus are a special case: they believed in time, and their faith protected them from a humiliating punishment.

The Qur'an does not name the city of Yunus and does not say how long he remained inside the fish, and we do not need to know.

Allah tells the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to be patient and not to be like the companion of the fish when he cried out in distress. He also says that his Lord chose Yunus and placed him among the righteous. His story therefore carries both a warning against impatience and great hope.
lesson: Do not give up on a duty out of frustration. And if you have slipped, no darkness is too deep: admit your mistake and call on Allah.

name: Zakariyya (Zechariah)
title: The servant who never despaired of his prayer
story:
Zakariyya, peace be upon him, was a prophet among the Children of Israel. The Qur'an presents him first as the guardian of Maryam, the mother of Isa, peace be upon them. She had been dedicated to the service of Allah, and Zakariyya was the one entrusted with her care.

Each time he came to see her in the place where she prayed, he found food with her. He asked her where it came from. She answered that it was from Allah, who provides for whom He wills without measure.

This answer touched him deeply. Zakariyya was a very old man, and his wife had never been able to have children. Yet, seeing the generosity of Allah towards Maryam, he turned to his Lord there and then and asked for a good child.

The Qur'an reports this prayer with tenderness. Zakariyya called upon his Lord in a low voice. He said that his bones had become weak and that his hair had turned white, but that he had never been disappointed when he prayed to Him. He was worried about those who would come after him, and he asked for an heir who would be pleasing to Allah. He also said: my Lord, do not leave me alone, and You are the best of inheritors.

The answer came while he was standing in prayer. The angels announced to him a son named Yahya, a name that Allah had not given to anyone before. He would be noble, chaste and a prophet from among the righteous.

Zakariyya was amazed: how could he have a son at his age, with a wife who could not bear children? He was told that this is easy for Allah, who does what He wills. He asked for a sign. The sign was that he would not speak to people for three days, except by gestures, although he was in good health. He came out to his people and signalled to them to glorify Allah morning and evening.

The Qur'an says that Allah answered him, gave him Yahya and cured his wife. It then explains why this family was honoured: they hastened to do good deeds, they called upon Allah with hope and fear, and they were humble before Him.
lesson: Keep asking Allah with hope, whatever your age or situation. The good you see in others can be an invitation to ask for more yourself.

name: Yahya (John)
title: Wise from childhood, gentle and pure
story:
Yahya, peace be upon him, is the son of Zakariyya, peace be upon him. He was born in answer to the prayer of his elderly father, when nothing seemed to make it possible. Allah Himself chose his name, and the Qur'an says that no one had been given this name before him.

The Qur'an does not tell the events of his life as a story. It gives instead a portrait of his character, in a few verses of Surah Maryam, and this portrait is one of the most beautiful in the Book.

Allah commanded him to hold firmly to the Scripture, and gave him wisdom while he was still a child. Yahya did not wait to grow old to take his faith seriously: from his earliest years, he understood what Allah asked of him and held on to it with strength.

Allah also gave him tenderness from Himself and purity. He feared Allah. He was dutiful to his parents, and he was neither arrogant nor disobedient. In Surah Al Imran, the angels announce him to Zakariyya as one who would confirm a word from Allah, and as noble, chaste and a prophet from among the righteous. Commentators explain that the word from Allah refers to Isa, peace be upon him, whose mission Yahya confirmed.

Elsewhere the Qur'an names Yahya with Zakariyya, Isa and Ilyas, and says that all of them were among the righteous. In the hadith about the Night Journey, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ relates that he met Yahya and Isa together in the second heaven, and that they were cousins (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3887).

The portrait ends with a greeting that Allah gives him: peace upon him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive. These are the three moments when a human being is most vulnerable, and Yahya is promised safety in each of them.

The Qur'an does not describe how Yahya called his people or how he died. Accounts of his death exist in other sources, but they are not found in the Qur'an, and we do not present them as certain.

Yahya shows that strength and gentleness go together. He was firm with the Scripture and soft with people, serious in his faith and kind to his parents.
lesson: You are never too young to take your faith and your values seriously. Be firm about what is right and gentle with people, starting with your parents.

name: Isa (Jesus)
title: The Messiah, son of Maryam
story:
Isa, peace be upon him, is one of the greatest messengers of Allah. The Qur'an calls him the Messiah, son of Maryam (Mary), and gives his mother a unique place: a whole surah bears her name.

Maryam was a pure and devout young woman. One day, when she had withdrawn from her family to worship, an angel appeared to her and announced that she would have a pure son. She was amazed: how could she have a child when no man had touched her? The angel answered that this is easy for Allah, who creates what He wills. When He decides a matter, He only says to it: Be, and it is.

Maryam gave birth alone, near the trunk of a palm tree, in pain and distress. She was comforted: a stream flowed beneath her, and fresh dates fell from the tree when she shook it.

When she returned to her people carrying the child, they accused her. She simply pointed to him. The newborn then spoke, by the permission of Allah. He said that he was the servant of Allah, that Allah had given him the Scripture and made him a prophet, had made him blessed wherever he was, and had enjoined on him prayer, charity and kindness to his mother.

Isa was sent as a messenger to the Children of Israel. He confirmed the Torah that came before him and received the Gospel. Allah supported him with clear signs: by the permission of Allah, he healed the blind and the leper, gave life to the dead, and shaped a bird from clay which became a living bird. The Qur'an repeats each time that these miracles happened by the permission of Allah.

His message was the same as that of all the prophets: Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; that is the straight path. His disciples believed in him and declared that they submitted to Allah. At their request, Isa prayed for a table spread with food to be sent down from heaven as a sign.

The Qur'an also says that Isa announced a messenger who would come after him. When his enemies plotted against him, the Qur'an teaches that they neither killed him nor crucified him, although it appeared so to them, and that Allah raised him to Himself.

Muslims love and honour Isa and his mother.
lesson: Honour your mother and stand by the truth with gentleness. True greatness lies in being a faithful servant of Allah and in bringing good wherever you are.

name: Muhammad ﷺ
title: The Seal of the Prophets, a mercy to the worlds
story:
The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born in Mecca around the year 570 CE, in the tribe of Quraysh. His father died before his birth and his mother when he was a small child, so he was raised by his grandfather, then by his uncle Abu Talib. As a young man, he was so honest that people called him al-Amin, the trustworthy. He married Khadija, may Allah be pleased with her, a respected merchant of Mecca.

He used to withdraw to the cave of Hira, on a mountain near Mecca, to reflect and to worship. There, when he was about forty years old, the angel Jibril (Gabriel) brought him the first words of the Qur'an, commanding him to read in the name of his Lord who created. Khadija was the first to believe in him.

For thirteen years he called the people of Mecca to worship Allah alone, to be honest, to care for orphans and the poor, and to give up idols. A few people followed him, but the leaders of Quraysh opposed him, and the believers suffered insults, boycott and persecution. He answered with patience.

In 622, he emigrated to the city of Yathrib, which became Medina. This journey, the Hijra, marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar. The Qur'an recalls how, hidden in a cave with his companion Abu Bakr, he told him not to grieve, for Allah was with them.

In Medina he built a mosque, joined the emigrants from Mecca and the people of Medina in brotherhood, and organised the life of a community. The Muslims had to defend themselves several times, and the Prophet ﷺ also concluded a truce with Quraysh. When it was broken, he returned to Mecca in the year 8 of the Hijra, almost without fighting. He forgave those who had fought him for years and removed the idols from the Kaaba. People then entered the religion of Allah in crowds.

In the year 10, he performed his farewell pilgrimage. At Arafat, he spoke to a great crowd: he reminded them that life, property and honour are sacred, called for the good treatment of women, and declared that old blood feuds and usury were abolished. It was during this pilgrimage that the verse announcing that the religion had been perfected was revealed.

He died in Medina in the year 11 of the Hijra, 632 CE. The Qur'an calls him the Messenger of Allah and the last of the prophets, sent as a mercy to the worlds.
lesson: Be trustworthy before you speak about faith: character opens hearts. When you have the upper hand, choose mercy and forgiveness.
